summary: Make an integer collection on your own, and do not call a built-in hash collection from the language. It must do three things: put an integer into the collection, retaining a single copy when that integer is put again; ask whether an integer is in the collection now, writing true if so and false if not; take an integer out of the collection, leaving everything as it was when the integer was already missing. Integers involved lie between 0 and 1000000. The combined number of operations lies between 1 and 10000.
notes: The left column is this sample's input text and the right column is the text the program should print. Comparison ignores trailing newlines.
